subject: Request: Pilot sponsorship and privacy-oriented credits for State Univ. Data Ethics Lab
messages:
From: Dr. Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@stateuni.edu>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: grants@dataethicslab.org
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot sponsorship ask — State Univ. Data Ethics Lab

Hi Tessa,

I'm Lisa, PI for the Data Ethics Lab at State University. We're preparing a 6‑month student-and-researcher pilot that evaluates privacy-preserving assistance workflows for social science surveys. The pilot will run across three courses (approx. 120 students) and two research studies. We need a hosted inference partner that can:

- Provide a 6‑month trial extension (we've used the standard student promo already)
- Offer a promo credit pool sufficient for development + pilot (estimate: $10k usage credit)
- Support VPC or dedicated tenancy recommendations for restricted datasets, and provide a short SOC2 / data retention note for our IRB packet

I attached a short SOW (Pilot_SOW.pdf) and included a link to our IRB application in the Drive. Would Redwood consider sponsoring credits and a trial extension for this pilot? We can acknowledge Redwood in course materials and a short write-up for the lab website.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call this week.

Best,

Lisa Chen, PhD
Director, Data Ethics Lab
State University
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Dr. Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@stateuni.edu>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot sponsorship ask — State Univ. Data Ethics Lab

Hi Lisa — thanks for the note and the SOW.

This sounds aligned with our education research support playbook. A few quick asks from our side to move this forward:

1) Can you share the IRB approval (or application receipt) and a short data flow diagram outlining what data is sent to inference (anonymized text only vs. any PII) — that helps our security/compliance triage.
2) Do you need a Hosted API promo (fastest) or would you prefer Dedicated capacity / VPC recommendations for the pilot? If you expect identifiable data, Dedicated or Private is usually required.
3) Timeline: when do classes start and when do you need the credits active?

I'm looping in Ben (sales engineering) and Neha (program approvals) to help size the credit pool and cover the legal/compliance checklist.

I can also propose a 30-minute slot next week to walk through the IRB packet.

—Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Partnerships Manager, Education & Research
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Dr. Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@stateuni.edu>, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot sponsorship ask — Pilot SOW and credits sizing

Thanks, Lisa and Tessa. I reviewed the SOW you attached and sketched a tentative credits proposal.

- Suggested promo credit allocation: $8,000 (hosted trial with monitoring + 30 days of extra run-time after demo period)
- If you need Dedicated/VPC: estimate $12,000 equivalent in committed credits to cover the reserved capacity overhead (we can convert to a temporary pilot discount)
- We typically require an IRB or institutional approval and an anonymization/data minimization plan before allocating Dedicated resources.

Can you confirm: course start date (for provisioning), expected average daily requests, and whether student submissions include any free-text responses that might contain names or PII? If the latter, we'll recommend a redaction step before sending to the model.

I've attached a draft SOW (SOW_draft.docx) that tweaks the milestones for integration, instructor training, and an end-of-pilot analysis.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Dr. Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@stateuni.edu>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 17 Nov 2026 09:26:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot sponsorship ask — IRB and data notes

Hi Tessa, Ben — thanks for the quick review.

Attached is our IRB approval PDF (IRB_approval.pdf). The student coursework uses anonymized free-text responses; we redact direct identifiers before export. The research studies have a signed consent with data handling described.

Course start date: Jan 11, 2027. Expected average: ~1,200 API calls/week during term ramp, peak ~2,500 requests/week for instructor review sessions.

Drive link with the IRB packet and data flow diagram: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3CexampleDRIVE

We'd prefer Hosted API credits if possible for speed of setup; however, if the SOC2/retention note suggests Dedicated, we're open to guidance. Also happy to include Redwood branding on our lab site and share a short case study at pilot end.

Best,
Lisa
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Dr. Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@stateuni.edu>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 17 Nov 2026 15:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot sponsorship ask — Approval and next steps

Lisa — appreciative of the IRB and the clear timeline. After internal review, we can approve a sponsored pilot with the following terms: 

- Promo credits: $8,000 hosted-credit allocation active Jan 4, 2027 — Jul 4, 2027 (6 months).
- Trial extension: 6 months (we'll extend the student promo window so the lab can finish the term).
- Compliance: Hosted API is acceptable given your redaction plan and IRB; we'll supply a short SOC2 summary and our data retention note for your IRB packet (see Drive attachment).
- Provisioning: Ben will create the project and provide API keys + monitoring dashboard.
- Legal: We'll send a short pilot addendum (DocuSign link) to formalize the credit grant and data terms — please have your grants office sign.

Neha — can you please confirm the promo allocation in the portal and issue the credit code? Ben — next steps to provision and deliver the SOW revision + dashboard link. Lisa — we will also add Redwood to your lab acknowledgment language; thank you for offering the case study.

Next steps: I'll share the DocuSign link in a separate email once Neha confirms the allocation. Looking forward to this collaboration.

—Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Partnerships Manager, Education & Research
Redwood Inference
